A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet. The starting network scores 0 because it ends every episode with DONE at once. The cause is clear: the target channels are rolled 4 columns, but a 1x1 stem plus two 3x3 convolutions only sees ±2 columns, so it can never match the target to the build. Placements then score mostly negative reward and DONE (reward 0) wins. The first fix is a learned layer that sees the whole row with wraparound: a convolution whose kernel spans the full width, on input padded circularly. This learns the alignment rather than hard-coding a roll of 4, so it should also work on other grid sizes and shifts. The budget is small: the default recipe gives only about 25–32 PPO updates. So more frequent, smaller updates may matter. Plan: A tests the alignment layer alone with the default recipe. B adds faster updates. C also mixes along the y axis, to see whether that more general fix costs anything.

### Round 2
The starting network scored 0 because its 3x3 convolutions never see the target cells, which the observation shifts 4 columns away. A full-row circular convolution fixed this (0.085). Updating twice as often (64 envs × 32 steps) raised the 2-seed mean to 0.22, but the seeds scored 0.08 and 0.37, so that gain is noisy. Axial mixing also scored 0.22, with seeds closer together (0.20 and 0.25), so it is the best so far. In the traces the agent is precise: about 0.35 cells per episode land outside the target, against about 19 inside. It fails by stopping early and leaving out upper layers and overhangs that need support built first. Training success was still rising at the end (0.08 at 75%, 0.18 at 100%), and each trial took only about 60 of its 900 seconds. That points to too few samples, not too little time. Next: buy more samples with fewer PPO epochs or a cheaper exact alignment layer, and try a longer reward horizon to help ordering.

### Round 3
Learned full-span circular mixing solves the hidden 4-column shift. RowMix and Axial both reach about 0.22, while the starting network and a weak per-channel permutation collapse to DONE (0.00). Collapse to an immediate DONE is the main failure mode. It also hit Axial with 2 epochs on both seeds. The likely cause is a race: DONE is a safe action worth 0, while the placements that earn reward need aligned features. Variance between seeds is large (0.08 vs 0.37). Successful runs place almost nothing outside the target (IoU about 0.79) but stop with DONE too early, leaving towers and upper layers unfinished. Training success was still rising at the end, so the runs seem short of learning. A longer horizon did not help (0.15). Next tests: more gradient steps at the same compute (smaller minibatches), entropy against collapse, and a leaner network under 1x compute for about 1.4x more samples.

### Round 4
The main barrier was the hidden 4-column shift. Full-span circular axial mixing (rowmix plus colmix) solved it: starting from 0, these runs place about 99% of their cells inside the target. All the gains since then came from the training recipe. Frequent updates (64 environments × 32 steps) helped. Two epochs and the 1x lean network both collapsed toward DONE or weak results. A longer horizon did not help. Two changes each raised the best seed: an entropy coefficient of 0.03 (r3c2, 0.37, the best mean) and 64-sample minibatches (r3c1, 0.457 on one seed). Seed variance is still about ±0.15, so single comparisons are weak. In the traces the agent places correct bricks but stops with DONE before upper layers and some columns are complete, and training success was still rising at the end. More optimiser progress per sample and continued exploration look like the levers. With 3 trials left, I am combining and extending the two changes that helped on the best network.

## Trial it ended with
name: Axial + ent0.03 + 90 short updates
hypothesis: Same as r3c2 (entropy 0.03), but each update collects 64 environments × 16 steps and splits them into 16 minibatches of 64 samples. That gives about 90 PPO updates instead of 45, with twice the Adam steps and fresher policies. Earlier, more frequent updates helped (r1c2 over r1c1), and training was still rising at the end. Refuted if dev success is at or below 0.37. A collapse of either seed would mean the shorter rollouts give GAE estimates that are too noisy.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).
